title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout / Go-Live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing rollout plan for the pilot -> production cutover. Discussed canary percentages, A/B strategy, monitoring dashboards, rollback/runbook items, perf targets (p95 < 220ms for inference), and security checks (SOC2 artifacts, KMS). Agreed on dry run and timeline for canary ramp, plus owners for runbook, infra provisioning, and post-cutover validation.

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (AtlasRetail - Head of ML), Jordan Reed (AtlasRetail - SRE), Priya Nair (AtlasRetail - Product)

Summary: quick run through of the canary plan, monitoring, runbooks, and dry-run timing. A few action items captured at the end.

[00:00] Avery: okay everyone, thanks for joining, let's kick off — this is our weekly POC sync focused on rollout and go-live planning. Samir and I are here from Redwood. Maya, Jordan, Priya, you on?
[00:12] Maya: yep here, thanks. we reviewed the last week's perf numbers — looked good — but want to make sure the cutover plan covers rollback triggers.
[00:20] Samir: quick reminder of goals — p95 latency under 250ms for the pilot traffic and error rate < 0.5%. we suggested p95 target at 220ms to give headroom.
[00:32] Jordan: can you remind us of the difference between the dedicated run and the hosted fallback in this plan? if we see a node gap what happens?
[00:40] Avery: yes — primary will be Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs). fallback is hosted API on a lower tier model variant. routing policy will auto-failover if capacity drops below threshold, and we keep a canary route to catch degradation.
[00:55] Maya: for data handling we need to confirm KMS integration and no token logs in the hosted path — we flagged compliance.
[01:03] Samir: KMS is supported in Private deploy and Dedicated via customer-managed KMS for keys. Hosted path will have redacted logs; we can provide SOC2 docs. we'll add a step in the runbook to verify encryption and audit log presence in staging.
[02:15] Priya: timeline check — our product deadline is end of month; what's a realistic canary ramp schedule?
[02:24] Avery: proposed: day 0 dry run (small internal traffic), day 1 start canary 5% for 4 hours, if stable ramp to 25% next day, then 50% and full 100% after validation. with rollback windows after each step.
[02:36] Jordan: 5% seems small. can we do functionality A/B at 10% and measure quality and latency against control?
[02:44] Samir: yes, we can do A/B — route 10% of real traffic to Redwood inference and keep 90% to the control path. we'll capture quality metrics (BLEU-ish/semantic similarity) and perf.
[03:00] Maya: how do we evaluate quality automatically? we need guardrails so product doesn't regress.
[03:05] Samir: we'll run a prompt set of the 20 critical prompts Maya provides; responses go through a lightweight evaluator (semantic similarity + heuristics). if quality metric drops below threshold, automatic rollback. add this to the playbook.
[04:10] Avery: let's talk triggers: example triggers — p95 latency increase > 30% vs baseline, error rate > 1%, quality score drop > 5% absolute, or any data leakage alert. if any trigger, immediate rollback to prev variant and alert oncall.
[04:25] Jordan: for rollback, what is the expected RTO? we need a runbook step that lists who clicks what.
[04:30] Samir: RTO depends on the route — we can rollback at router level within 30s, but downstream cache/warmth may take a few minutes. runbook will list manual confirmation steps and an automated circuit breaker that flips traffic.
[05:05] Priya: who is the oncall? I want to map names — product, SRE, Redwood SE.
[05:10] Maya: we'll use our SRE rotation — Jordan oncall for the dry run, Priya will be product lead, Avery/Samir Redwood oncall backup.
[06:00] Avery: monitoring — Samir, can you walk through the dashboards and alerts you recommend?
[06:05] Samir: yep. Dashboard 1: latency time series (p50, p95, p99), request rate, token cost per call. Dashboard 2: quality signals (similarity score distribution vs baseline), KV cache hit rate, token savings. Alert rules: p95 > 220ms for 5m, error rate > 0.5% for 3m, quality drop > 5% immediate. we'll provide Grafana + Redwood trace links.
[07:30] Jordan: token cost per call is important for budget — can you show expected cost delta at 10k calls/day?
[07:40] Samir: rough math — current hosted alternative costs X, Redwood Dedicated optimized path with caching reduces token cost by ~18% for similar workloads; I'll send a detailed sheet.
[08:10] Maya: security — confirm audit logs will be available, SSO SAML mapping, RBAC for the Redwood console.
[08:18] Avery: yes, we'll share the SOC2 pack and the RBAC guide; SAML SSO is supported and we can map roles to your AD groups. runbook will capture admin steps.
[09:00] Priya: dry run plan specifics? we need steps and timeline.
[09:05] Avery: dry-run (2026-06-18 10:00-12:00 UTC): 1) smoke tests against staging, 2) run the 20 critical prompts, 3) validate dashboard and alerts, 4) simulate degraded node and confirm failover, 5) verify rollback works. each step owner noted.
[10:30] Jordan: sim degraded node — can you simulate kernel OOM or GPU throttling?
[10:36] Samir: we can throttle GPU utilization in staging and force the routing policy to engage fallback. we'll also test KV cache cold start to observe latency spike and ensure autoscaler behaves.
[12:00] Maya: reporting frequency during canary? hourly or 15-min?
[12:05] Priya: for early canary, 15-min is better. we'll want hourly summaries once at 25%+.
[13:30] Avery: runbook section — cutover steps: pre-cutover checklist, canary ramp, verification checks, full cutover, post-cutover validation, rollback. prepping the post-cutover smoke tests is important.
[14:10] Jordan: pre-cutover checklist should include certs, KMS keys rotated, IP whitelists, synthetic monitoring checks green.
[14:22] Samir: noted — we will add verification hooks: KMS test decrypt, log ingestion check, trace sampling verification.
[15:00] Maya: data residency question — if traffic routes to hosted fallback in a different region will that violate policy?
[15:08] Avery: we can pin region routing; fallback can be restricted to same region or private fallback only. we'll make that configurable in policy.
[17:00] Priya: what about canary metrics for quality — do we store full responses for review? concerns about PII.
[17:08] Samir: store redacted responses in staging bucket, with PII removal regex and only authorized reviewers. we'll include a step to validate redaction before storing.
[19:00] Avery: ops — alerting channels: PagerDuty for high-sev, Slack for postmortem thread, and email to product for daily summaries.
[20:00] Jordan: agree. ensure runbook lists escalation matrix with phone numbers and Slack handles.
[22:00] Maya: okay, can we have a checklist for quality signoff? product signoff needs pass on all 20 prompts and no more than 1 regression allowed.
[22:10] Priya: will define the acceptance criteria and send by 2026-06-14.
[25:00] Samir: a note on performance tuning — we'll pre-warm KV cache for the first batch, and use batching policy tuned to your median prompt length. That reduces p95 by ~15% in our bench.
[27:00] Jordan: autoscaling config — we want limits to avoid runaway cost but still absorb spikes. what's recommended?
[27:10] Samir: set a min replica to maintain baseline throughput, and a hard max to cap cost. we'll propose values based on your 95th percentile QPS from the last 30 days.
[30:00] Avery: legal/procurement — do you need a temporary contract to run the pilot?
[30:08] Maya: procurement asked if there's a short-term addendum; procurement is okay with a 30-day eval with NDA and SOC2 evidence.
[31:00] Priya: can you share the security packet?
[31:05] Avery: yes, I'll send SOC2 Type II report, the KMS integration guide, and the RBAC docs after the call.
[33:00] Jordan: small nit — metrics alignment: please use our existing metric names for latency and errors so we can overlay easily.
[33:08] Samir: we'll export metrics with your naming convention — Samir to map metric names and share.
[35:00] Maya: any risk items we haven't covered?
[35:05] Avery: main risks — quality regression, unexpected cost if caching ineffective, and region/fallback residency issues. mitigation: conservative ramp, alerting, and pre-signed budgets.
[36:30] Priya: do we run canary on a subset of tenants or all tenants?
[36:40] Maya: tenant-based is preferred — start with internal tenants then expand to 2 low-risk customers.
[37:00] Samir: rollout will include tenant header routing so we can isolate by tenant id. add to runbook.
[38:00] Avery: communication plan — status updates on Slack channel #atlas-redwood-pilot during the dry run and canary. weekly exec summary after 100% cutover.
[39:00] Jordan: okay, can you list concrete rollback criteria again so it's clear?
[39:05] Samir: yes: automatic rollback if p95 latency > 30% of baseline OR error rate > 1% sustained for 3 minutes OR quality score drop > 5% absolute OR any data leakage alert. manual rollback if ops see issues.
[41:00] Priya: testing the canary metrics pipeline — how do we ensure the similarity evaluator is deterministic?
[41:10] Samir: evaluator is reproducible with seeded runs; for production we'll snapshot the evaluation model version and store seeds. add check in runbook.
[43:00] Avery: timeline recap and owners — quick round robin.
[43:10] Maya: Maya -> provide 20 critical prompts and success thresholds by 6/14.
[43:20] Jordan: Jordan -> staging VPC + test keys by 6/15, be oncall for dry run.
[43:30] Priya: Priya -> product acceptance criteria doc by 6/14, coordinate comms.
[43:40] Samir: Samir -> dashboards and metric mapping by 6/13.
[43:50] Avery: Avery -> send rollout runbook, SOC2 and security packet by 6/12, schedule dry run 6/18.
[45:00] Maya: sounds good. any other questions?
[45:05] Jordan: one more — during canary how do we handle backpressure from downstream services?
[45:12] Samir: we'll set circuit breakers and token bucket throttles; runbook has rate-limits per route and fallbacks.
[46:00] Priya: okay, capture these as action items.
[46:05] Avery: will do. we'll also include a short checklist for the oncall to run through during the first 30 minutes.
[48:00] Maya: thanks everyone — feel better about the plan.
[48:05] Avery: thanks — we'll follow up with the runbook and dashboards, and see you for the dry run on 6/18.
[48:15] Samir: bye all.

Recap (end): Action items and next steps agreed. Dry run scheduled 2026-06-18 10:00-12:00 UTC.
